prompt:
Design a 4-storey steel moment-resisting frame for a building in seismic zone with a design PGA of 0.25g (Type 1 spectrum, ground type C per EN 1998-1). The frame has 3 bays of 6m span and 3.5m storey heights. Columns are HEB 300 (S355) and beams are IPE 400 (S355). The structure is designed as a moment-resisting frame with behaviour factor q = 4.0 (DCM ductility class).

The design uses the lateral force method with a base shear of 420 kN distributed as inverted triangle over the height. The inter-storey drift check shows a maximum drift ratio of 1.2% at the first floor under the design seismic action. The beam-to-column connections are full-strength welded moment connections with column web stiffeners. Please review the seismic design.

seeded_faults.description: The strong column-weak beam (SCWB) capacity design rule per EN 1998-1 Clause 4.4.2.3(4) requires ΣMRc ≥ 1.3 × ΣMRb at every beam-column joint (where MRc includes the effect of axial load). For HEB 300 columns (Wpl,y = 1678 cm³) and IPE 400 beams (Wpl,y = 1307 cm³): column moment capacity ≈ 1678 × 355/1000 = 595.7 kN·m per column, beam moment capacity ≈ 1307 × 355/1000 = 464.0 kN·m per beam. At an interior joint with 2 columns and 2 beams: ΣMRc/ΣMRb = (2 × 595.7)/(2 × 464.0) = 1.28, which is LESS than the required 1.3. The SCWB check marginally fails. With axial load reducing column capacity, the actual ratio will be lower still. This risks formation of a soft-storey collapse mechanism.
seeded_faults.location_hint: HEB 300 columns with IPE 400 beams in a moment frame designed for DCM ductility.

seeded_faults.description: The inter-storey drift limit for buildings with brittle non-structural elements (brick/block infills, glazed facades) is 0.5% × ν per EN 1998-1 Clause 4.4.3.2, where ν is a reduction factor (typically 0.5 for Importance Class II). This gives an allowable drift of 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25% under the design seismic action. Even for ductile non-structural elements, the limit is 0.75% × ν = 0.375%. The reported 1.2% drift vastly exceeds both limits. If the 1.2% is the drift under the reduced (design) forces, the actual drift at the design displacement would be approximately q × 1.2% × ν = potentially much larger. Either the drift is misreported or the frame is far too flexible and requires larger sections or bracing.
seeded_faults.location_hint: Maximum inter-storey drift ratio of 1.2% reported as acceptable.

ground_truth_notes: Two faults: (1) SCWB check per EN 1998-1 Cl. 4.4.2.3(4) requires ΣMRc ≥ 1.3 × ΣMRb. With HEB 300/IPE 400, the ratio is 1.28 before axial load reduction — fails the 1.3 threshold. (2) Inter-storey drift limit per EN 1998-1 Cl. 4.4.3.2 is 0.5% × ν for brittle elements (0.25% with ν=0.5), or 0.75% × ν for ductile (0.375%). 1.2% vastly exceeds all limits. Reference: BS EN 1998-1:2004+A1:2013.
